why: Check 1's expect line only requires that --tsv output is "the same JSON array" the CSV run prints for the same table. Its PASS condition adds that the output must equal a hard-coded literal, "[{"name":"ann","age":"30","city":"oslo"},{"name":"bob","age":"","city":"rome"}]". Its FAIL condition fails if the output "is not that JSON array". That tests what the existing CSV parser outputs, which the words don't require. If the CSV path printed something else (e.g. numbers), TSV and CSV could still match and the check would fail anyway. "Byte-identical" via cmp is also stricter than "same JSON array". These belong under Advisory. Check 2 (grep plus a description of what the flag does) fits "documents --tsv", and the Advisory section is placed correctly. Because Check 1 adds tests the words don't require, the criterion fails.
